newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money eases at close, gilts inactive.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money eases at close, gilts inactive.

text.p: Indian call money eased slightly in late trade to end Monday at 10.75 percent, off the day's high of 11.25 percent, dealers said. It opened the day in the 10.75-11.0 percent range.
They said demand for funds came down slightly in the afternoon, leading to a marginal drop in rates.
"The 11 percent barrier remains a major resistance level," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "It is likely to be breached only if a majority of banks exhaust their export refinance limits."
Banks can get refinance from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) against their export credit disbursals at a rate of 11 percent per annum.
Dealers said there were no trades in the securities market on Monday.
"The market was completely dead today," said a dealer. "Market players are awaiting the results of the securiites auction."
The RBI auctions 20 billion rupees of three-year gopvernment of India securities later on Monday.
Dealers said the yield at the auction would provide a crucial indication on the direction of interest rates in the immediate future.

"The RBI has two choices," said a dealer. "Either it fixes a high yield and mops up the major portion of the 20 billion rupees from the market or it chooses a low yield in keeping with its aim of reducing interest rates...in this case it may have to pick up a good portion of the stock itself."
Dealers said no trades were reported in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
